stem: A client cannot actively move the affected extremity after orthopedic surgery, and passive range-of-motion exercises have been prescribed. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Support the extremity and move the joint slowly and gently through the prescribed passive range, stopping at pain or firm resistance rather than forcing additional motion.
options.B: Move the joint through the full normal range at each session even when resistance is felt, because reaching the expected anatomic range is the goal of passive ROM.
options.C: Use the same passive-ROM sequence and range for all postoperative clients, then increase the range when the joint feels looser even if the rehabilitation plan has not changed.
options.D: Keep the extremity completely at rest until the client can assist actively, because prescribed passive ROM should be deferred when the client cannot produce joint movement independently.

rationale: Current NCBI Open RN guidance defines passive range of motion as joint movement produced by another person while the client remains relaxed. The Nursing Assistant text directs the caregiver to support the limb, move the joint gently only to slight resistance, never force a joint through resistance, and observe for pain. Nursing Fundamentals further states that ROM is prescribed and should be performed slowly and gently according to the prescribed plan. Therefore A is correct. B forces movement beyond resistance, C substitutes an unapproved standardized and self-progressed range for the individualized prescription, and D contradicts the purpose of prescribed passive ROM when the client cannot actively produce the movement.
educational_objective: Perform prescribed passive range of motion by supporting the extremity and moving the joint slowly and gently within the prescribed range, while avoiding forced movement through pain or resistance.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf; Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN)
source_document_title: Nursing Assistant — Chapter 9: Promote Independence Through Rehabilitation/Restorative Care; Nursing Fundamentals — Chapter 13 Mobility; Nursing Skills — Chapter 13 Musculoskeletal Assessment
source_version_date: Nursing Assistant 2022; Nursing Fundamentals 2021; Nursing Skills 2nd edition 2023; current NCBI Bookshelf versions accessed 2026-08-25
source_locator: Nursing Assistant > Chapter 9 > Range of Motion (ROM): support the limb around the joint; move the joint gently only to the point of slight resistance; never force full ROM when resistance is present; observe and ask about pain. Nursing Fundamentals > Chapter 13 > Range of Motion Exercises: ROM may be prescribed after injury or surgery; exercises are prescribed by physical therapy and can be performed by nursing personnel according to agency policy; passive stretching should be performed slowly and gently. Nursing Skills > Chapter 13 > Musculoskeletal Assessment > Palpation: stabilize/support the joint and gently move it through passive ROM; pain or tenderness with movement is not expected.
source_claim_supported: Prescribed passive ROM is performed with the client relaxed, the limb supported, and the joint moved slowly and gently without forcing through pain or resistance; the exercise range and progression follow the prescribed rehabilitation plan.

supporting_sources.organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf; Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN)
supporting_sources.version_date: 2021 text; current NCBI Bookshelf version accessed 2026-08-25
supporting_sources.locator: Range of Motion Exercises: passive ROM is movement applied by another person while the client remains relaxed; ROM can be prescribed after injury or surgery; ROM is prescribed by physical therapy and may be performed by nurses according to policy; stretching is performed slowly and gently.
supporting_sources.claim_supported: Passive ROM is an individualized prescribed intervention and should be performed slowly and gently.

supporting_sources.organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf; Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN)
supporting_sources.locator: Palpation: when active ROM is decreased, stabilize the joint with one hand and gently move it passively with the other; pain or tenderness should not occur with normal movement.
supporting_sources.claim_supported: Support/stabilization and gentle movement are appropriate passive-ROM technique, with pain requiring reassessment rather than forced motion.

blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort, printed pp. 35–36: related activity statement 'Implement measures to promote circulation (e.g., active or passive range of motion, positioning and mobilization)'; Mobility/Immobility includes applying nursing procedures and psychomotor skills for clients with immobility, maintaining correct body alignment, implementing active or passive ROM, and evaluating client response to interventions preventing immobility complications.
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — safe performance of prescribed passive range-of-motion exercises
correction_summary: Rebuilt all four actions to remove the absolute-word pattern and uniquely-long keyed answer. The revised distractors test realistic errors: forcing through resistance, independently standardizing/progressing the prescribed range, and withholding passive movement merely because the client cannot assist actively.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Postoperative mobility support — prescribed passive range of motion
audit_findings.stem: PASS — clearly establishes inability to move actively and an existing passive-ROM prescription, so the construct is safe execution rather than deciding whether ROM should be ordered.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS — directly matches current NCBI/Open RN technique: support the limb, move slowly and gently, follow the prescribed range, and do not force painful or resistant movement; uniquely best.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS as distractor — full anatomical range can sound desirable, but forcing through resistance conflicts with direct ROM technique guidance.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — consistency is useful in rehabilitation, but using an identical range for all postoperative clients and self-progressing beyond the current plan violates individualized prescription.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS as distractor — inability to move actively is precisely a circumstance in which passive ROM may be prescribed, so deferring it solely for lack of active assistance contradicts the prescribed intervention.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — A is the only option that executes the existing prescription without adding force, unapproved progression, or unjustified withholding.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — B forces resistance, C self-progresses the prescription, and D withholds prescribed passive movement.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — choices are similar in length and clinical detail; the keyed answer is no longer uniquely longest or associated with a keyed-only absolute term.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Basic Care and Comfort explicitly includes active/passive ROM and mobility interventions for immobility.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether a fuller range or delaying until active participation could ever be reasonable; the stem already states passive ROM is prescribed, and current Open RN guidance says to move gently only to resistance and never force, leaving A uniquely correct.
